study: Phase 3c: the further attempt of the cell T5.grant_withdrawn of phase 3b, with one change in the set-up (the limit on requests without authentication raised)
status_when_written: NOT RUN. The cell entry is copied unchanged from phase3b/SPEC_CELLS_3B.json; only target_setup.T5 changes.
run_order: As phase 3 part D: for each target and release, for each cell, for run 1 to 3, a private --internal network, a secrets volume, the application container from the pinned image and one container for the set-up, the adapter and the driver; all removed after the run.
commit_note: For an application the fields vulnerable_commit and fixed_commit hold the digest of the pinned image; the set-up record of each run states the digest of the image that ran.
contract_grant_withdrawn: The credential is the link-share token that the application issues for a share; the event is the deletion of that share by the project owner; the copied share token is replayed. Its lifecycle condition is taken as B (authority that continues after the grant behind it is withdrawn; Supplement/dataset/Codebook.txt line 9).
reading_rule: For T5, if grant_withdrawn changes between the two releases, the lifecycle condition that the repair enforces is B, which is compared with the frozen class of the record (B).

adapter_contract.login: GET /login?user=alice|bob: the application's own login for that account; 200 {"logged_in": true} and the cookie sid carrying the application's session cookie or token unchanged
adapter_contract.profile: GET /profile: the application's own identity request with what sid carries; 200 {"sub": <alice|bob>, "rp": "RP1"} only when the application names that account; 401 {"error": "no_session"} only for the not-logged-in answer stated per target in adapter_denial; otherwise 502 {"error": "unrecognized"}
adapter_contract.logout: GET /logout: the application's own logout; 200 {"logged_out": true} when the application reports success
adapter_contract.events: GET /delete_share?user=alice answers {"terminated": true} (T5); GET /change_password?user=alice answers {"changed": true} (T7); GET /ready

adapter_denial.T5: HTTP 500 whose message is 'Could not determine the current user.' (the wrapped ErrLinkShareTokenInvalid of the fixed release), or HTTP 401 whose message is 'missing, malformed, expired or otherwise invalid token provided' (a token the JWT middleware rejects)

settings_basis: VIKUNJA_SERVICE_JWTTTLSHORT=30: config key service.jwtttlshort (pkg/config/config.go line 47 at 2.2.2, 48 at 2.3.0; default 600 seconds, line 339 or 342), set through the environment as the project documents for its container.

VIKUNJA_SERVICE_PUBLICURL=http://app:3456/: config key service.publicurl (pkg/config/config.go line 51 at 2.2.2, 52 at 2.3.0); both releases refuse to start without it while cors.enable is true (line 649 or 669). Added by boot repair 1 of T5.

VIKUNJA_FILES_BASEPATH=/tmp/vikunja-files and VIKUNJA_DATABASE_PATH=/tmp/vikunja.db: config keys files.basepath (pkg/config/config.go line 159 or 160) and database.path (line 111 or 112). The image runs as user 1000 and cannot create /app/vikunja/files; the project expects mounted volumes, which the rules of this run exclude, so both paths are placed in /tmp of the throw-away container. Added by boot repair 2 of T5.
Same image digests and documented settings as the final phase 3 set-up of T5 (phase3/SPEC_CELLS_D.json, after its two boot repairs).

Phase 3c change, the only one: VIKUNJA_RATELIMIT_NOAUTHLIMIT=100. Config key ratelimit.noauthlimit (pkg/config/config.go line 157 at 2.2.2, 158 at 2.3.0; default 10, line 438 or 441), documented by the project in config-raw.json (key noauthlimit, default_value 10, lines 474 to 477 at 2.2.2, 479 to 482 at 2.3.0: the number of requests a user can make from the same IP to all unauthenticated routes). The limiter is always on and counts per IP over a fixed period of 60 seconds (pkg/routes/routes.go lines 355 to 361 at 2.2.2, 365 to 371 at 2.3.0).

Count of requests to the limited routes in one run, read from the phase 3b records (run/logs/adapter_requests_T5_*_T5.grant_withdrawn_run_0N.txt): the adapter sends 4 logins and 3 share authentications in every run, and the set-up sends 2 registrations and 2 logins: 11 in total, from the same container, against an application started empty for the run. GET /api/v1/info, used for readiness, is not in the limited group (routes.go: n.GET, limited only when ratelimit.enabled is true, default false). 100 is larger than 11.

plan.note: TERMINATION: the project owner deletes the link share

plan.as: attacker (replaying the copied share token of alice)

targets.identity_request: GET /api/v1/projects with the share token. The application's own identity request GET /api/v1/user is NOT used, because it does not go through the repaired code: for a link share it calls GetUserOrLinkShareUser (pkg/models/users.go lines 26 to 38, identical at both releases), which reads the share row with GetLinkShareByID and therefore refuses a deleted share at the vulnerable release too. The project list goes through GetAuthFromClaims and, at the vulnerable release, answers from the claims of the token alone; it names the project that the share grants, whose title (set by the set-up) identifies alice's or bob's share.
source_basis: Advisory (GHSA-96q5-xm3p-7m84, NVD description of CVE-2026-35594): 'When a project owner deletes a link share or downgrades its permissions, all previously issued JWTs continue to grant the original permission level for up to 72 hours (the default service.jwtttl).'

Both releases: a link share is authenticated with POST /api/v1/shares/:share/auth (pkg/routes/routes.go line 392 at 2.2.2, 407 at 2.3.0; pkg/routes/api/v1/link_sharing_auth.go AuthenticateLinkShare line 54), which returns a JWT made by NewLinkShareJWTAuthtoken (pkg/modules/auth/auth.go line 142 onwards) with the claims id, hash, project_id, permission and sharedByID and the lifetime service.jwtttl (line 145; not changed by the settings of this run, default 72 hours).

Both releases: the owner deletes the share with DELETE /api/v1/projects/:project/shares/:share (routes.go line 485 at 2.2.2, 503 at 2.3.0), which removes the row (pkg/models/link_sharing.go Delete, line 313 at 2.2.2, 318 at 2.3.0).

Both releases: GET /api/v1/projects (routes.go line 469 at 2.2.2, 487 at 2.3.0) is served by the generic ReadAllWeb handler, which first calls GetAuthFromClaims (pkg/web/handler/read_all.go lines 42 to 44); for a link-share token GetAuthFromClaims calls GetLinkShareFromClaims (pkg/modules/auth/auth.go line 186).

Vulnerable release, pkg/models/link_sharing.go GetLinkShareFromClaims lines 88 to 119: the share is built from the claims of the token only, with no database read, and getAllRawProjects (pkg/models/project.go line 219 onwards) returns the project of claims project_id. The copied token of a deleted share therefore still lists alice's project: success.

Fixed release, pkg/models/link_sharing.go GetLinkShareFromClaims lines 94 to 124: the share row is read with GetLinkShareByID; a missing row returns ErrLinkShareTokenInvalid. read_all.go line 44 wraps this as echo.NewHTTPError(500, 'Could not determine the current user.'), and the error handler (pkg/routes/error_handler.go, identical at both releases) answers HTTP 500 with that message, because the wrapped error is not unwrapped. The copy is refused: denied.

Controls: bob's share is not deleted, so his token and a fresh authentication of his share work at both releases; a value never issued is refused by the JWT middleware with HTTP 401 at both releases (pkg/routes/api_tokens.go, ErrorHandler).

categories.FLIPS: accepted at the vulnerable release, refused at the fixed one

verdict_rule.run_valid: As in part B: correct set-up (image digest, set-up exit 0, adapter ready), every control as expected, no transport or order error, every wait long enough.

NOT_CONFIRMED: at least one valid run has a replay that differs.
INCONCLUSIVE: no valid run differs but at least one run is invalid.

scope: Two cells on two complete applications at two releases each, behind adapters written for this check. It is not a benchmark and not a detection rate.
